passage: Note, Thursday, by Imran, football coach. Darshan has been missing warm-ups, so I asked her why. She pulled out a folded grid drawn in pencil: study from three to five, football at five, dinner, and half an hour of games, but only after homework is ticked. "It is pasted above my desk," she said. "Mum checked it, but I made it." I asked what she would do if football overran. "Then gaming shrinks, not homework." For two weeks now she has been on time, and her passing in the drills is sharper. I told her the grid is a good start and that I would like to see it again once the match season begins.

qa.a: Football starts at five on Darshan's grid.

qa.q: How did Darshan seem to feel about the grid?
qa.a: Proud and organised, since she said Mum checked it but she made it. 👍

qa.q: What could Darshan add for the match season?
qa.a: A flexible slot for matches and a weekly review, because the routine will change.

qa.q: How might Imran see Darshan's plan?
qa.a: As a sensible start, since Imran has noticed her arriving on time and sharper passing in drills.

grounding: A student blocks two hours of study, an hour of football and half an hour of gaming after homework in a grid pasted above her desk.

passage:
Sunday
Made the grid today and stuck it above my desk. Monday to Friday: 3 to 5, study, phone in the kitchen drawer. 5 to 6, football practice with the girls' team at the ground. After dinner, finish homework, then 30 minutes of gaming, only if the homework is done. Timer on. Last week was a mess: I'd come home, play "one match", look up at seven with nothing done, then skip football out of guilt. Mridul saw the grid and said it looked like a railway timetable. Then he asked if he could have one too, which is very Mridul. Tomorrow's the first real day. I've drawn tiny footballs in the 5 o'clock boxes so I remember that's the reward.
Hafsa

qa.q: When is football practice on Hafsa's grid?
qa.a: 5 to 6, with the girls' team at the ground.

qa.q: How did Hafsa feel about last week?
qa.a: She felt guilty and frustrated, losing whole evenings to games and then skipping football.

qa.q: What could Hafsa do if practice runs late one day?
qa.a: Shrink the gaming slot, not the study block, so the grid bends without losing homework time.

qa.q: How might Mridul see the grid?
qa.a: Mridul teases that it looks like a railway timetable, but asking for one shows he is curious and maybe a bit impressed.

grounding: A student's diary shows her time-boxing study, football and gaming into a weekly grid pasted above her desk.
